Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

obisindicators 0.12.1

  • The monthly obis-h3 upload writes both stores (Ocean Metrics build week 6). New data-raw/publish_obis_h3.sh uploads a staged release on the host through oceanmetrics/platform scripts/om-publish.sh: the release folder, a count check on S3 and R2, then latest.json, then the stable collection.json, to R2 oceanmetrics-io-public-enam (served by storage.oceanmetrics.io) and S3 oceanmetrics.io-public, never deleting, the replaced R2 copies of the two pointers kept under obis-h3/_history/<date>/. refresh_obis_h3.sh gains OBIS_UPLOAD=host (stage only; aws, the S3-only upload, stays the default when it runs alone) and run_refresh_docker.sh sets it and runs the host upload after the container, so the R2 keys never enter the image.
  • refresh_obis_h3.sh’s PUBLIC_BASE (the root of the hrefs in latest.json and collection.json, and where the previous release is read) defaults to https://storage.oceanmetrics.io/obis-h3, so the next release keeps the storage-host hrefs the published files carry since the cutover of 2026-10-23.

obisindicators 0.12.0

  • species_flat per resolution. obis_h3_export_parquet() writes species_flat/res=1.parquet and res=2.parquet beside res=3.parquet (res_species_flat now defaults to 1:3): the finest resolution comes from the store as before (with h3), each coarser one is it rolled up, one row per cell and species with n summed, year_min the least and year_max the greatest (NULL only when every year is NULL), so a res-1 hexagon reads its own rows instead of its res-3 children’s. The roll-up files have the columns cell_id, name_key, aphiaid, n, year_min, year_max (no h3). New exported obis_h3_species_rollup_sql() (the roll-up, equal to obis_h3_species_sql() at that resolution straight from the store) and obis_h3_write_species_flat().
  • The res-3 species table split by res-1 parent: species_flat/res=3/p=<res-1 parent>.parquet, one file per parent with records, without the h3 column, sorted by cell_id, aphiaid in row groups of split_row_group_rows (default 2048; at most 2 x, as DuckDB writes them: 4,081 rows in v20261012) with cell_id statistics, so a cell’s file is small enough for its footer to come with the first range read. The files union to res=3.parquet, which is kept. New arguments species_flat_split (default c("3" = 1L), resolution = parent resolution; NULL for none) and split_row_group_rows. release.json layers.species_flat gains template_parent, parent_template, parent_res, by_res and split; files.parquet gives each split file’s parent.
  • The species lookup carries each species’ EOV and its lineage has a file of its own. species/species.parquet gains eov: the EOV whose layer counts the aphiaid, the store’s eov table joined on taxonID = aphiaid as the eov/ layers join occ_h3 (obis_h3_species_eov_sql()); NULL when no EOV counts it, and the column is left out when the store has no eov table. The seeds are disjoint subtrees of one tree, so an aphiaid is in one EOV at most; an aphiaid in two is an error, not a choice. species/lineage.parquet holds aphiaid, name_key, lineage only, sorted by aphiaid, so a WoRMS subtree reads the lineage without the names. Both are written in row groups of row_group_rows (obis_h3_write_species_lookup()). No redlist_code column: the store’s occ_h3 and taxon tables carry no IUCN Red List field (the OBIS snapshot’s interpreted.redlist_category is not brought into the store).
  • obis_h3_amend_species() adds these files to a release built by 0.11 in place: the lookup rewritten with eov (same rows, same order), the lineage file, the roll-ups and the split from the existing res=3.parquet (not rewritten), release.json and files.parquet (the new files added, every other row kept). Used to amend v20261012.
  • The collection describes them. obis_h3_stac_collection() lists obis:species.flat at every flat resolution with the split’s parent_template (species_flat/res={res}/p={parent}.parquet), parent_res and the columns of each file, obis:species.lineage, obis:species.eov, and the assets species_flat_res<r> and species_lineage; obis_h3_stac_stable() makes those hrefs absolute. The h3 profile 1.1 closes h3:species_table (no keys beyond its seven), so the flat files stay described under obis:species.flat, where the atlas reads them; h3:species_table is unchanged.

obisindicators 0.11.0

  • Every indicator layer file is sorted by cell_id in small row groups. obis_h3_export_parquet() gains row_group_rows (default 10000; DuckDB row groups are at most 2 x row_group_rows; DuckDB rounds to 2,048-row vectors: 12,045 rows at most in v20261012) and writes each file of the all, eov, taxon, decade and year layers with its own sorted COPY (obis_h3_write_partitions(), order_by = "cell_id"), so the cell_id statistics of consecutive row groups are disjoint and a reader that knows the cells under a tile range-reads only those groups. DuckDB’s PARTITION_BY wrote the groups out of order (the v20261012 all/res=5 file had 6 groups of up to 122,880 rows, not in cell_id order). The paths are unchanged (the explicit writer encodes partition values as DuckDB did: all 7,370 v20261012 taxon paths compare equal). release.json records sorted_by, row_group_rows and row_group_rows_max (the largest group written). max_open is no longer used. stats.parquet is written in row groups of row_group_rows too (sorted by layer, key, so a legend reads only its layer’s groups; the v20261012 file’s first 122,880-row group held all, eov and half the taxa).
  • The heads are built, as taxon layers. obis_h3_export_parquet() writes the taxa of species/heads.json (Animalia and every taxon spanning two or more named classes) under the existing taxon/rank=<rank>/taxon=<name>/res=<r>/ layout at res_heads (default 1-7, res 6 and 7 split by parent_res_taxon), so a reader draws a head as any taxon layer and never reads the class files; they are in stats.parquet, taxon_groups.parquet and files.parquet like the rank layers. rank is the WoRMS rank lowercased without a botanical alias (kingdom, subphylum, superclass; “Phylum (Division)” is phylum). New exported obis_h3_heads_sql(): the WoRMS subtree over the lookup’s lineage, species counted by name_key, so a head equals obis_h3_species_subtree_sql() cell for cell (tested at res 3-5, and against h3t’s recursive-CTE subtree at res 1-7). A head is not written when a layer already serves it: a subtree holding every aphiaid is the all layer (Biota: equal to all cell for cell at res 4 on v20261012), and a head whose rank and name are a rank layer keeps that layer, which is built from the OBIS rank column (the 40 phyla among the v20261012 heads; Chordata’s phylum layer differs from its WoRMS subtree in 1,967 of 173,824 res-4 cells). heads.json gives each head’s served_by (head, all, rank_layer, homonym) and layer; release.json gets layers.taxon.heads and layers.species.heads.n_built. New arguments heads (default TRUE) and res_heads.
  • The species table carries the first and last year. obis_h3_species_sql() and every species file gain year_min and year_max (SMALLINT; the first and last year the aphiaid was recorded in the cell, NULL when no record has a year; within the decade in the decade variant), for the Cell pane.
  • The decade species table is on by default, at res 3 and 4: species_decades now defaults to TRUE and the new res_species_decade (default c(3, 4)) sets its resolutions (it followed res_species before), for the decade filter on a WoRMS subtree. layers.species_decade in release.json lists its resolutions, decades and columns (with period = "decade").
  • species_flat/res=<r>.parquet: the species table in one file per resolution for every class, sorted by cell_id, aphiaid in row groups of row_group_rows, so the species of a cell are a range read of one file (spike 2: 0.53 MB read for a res-1 cell against 5.3 MB from the class files). New argument res_species_flat (default 3); release.json gets layers.species_flat.
  • Exact species per place. obis_place_indicators_exact() returns species (new argument species = TRUE): one row per place x aphiaid x name_key with n records and year_min, year_max, from the same point-in-polygon pass as the indicators, so the Place page’s species list is the record and not the H3 cells’ (the species’ n sum to the place’s n, and its distinct name_key count is its sp). New argument lookup (the release’s species/species.parquet, a path or a data frame) gives the release’s name_key by name, so the rows join the lookup; a name it lacks gets a key above its largest. obis_place_exact_write() writes place_exact/coll=<coll>/species.parquet (place_id, aphiaid, name_key, n, year_min, year_max, most records first) and counts it in meta.json; obis_h3_add_place_exact() lists it in files.parquet and adds its template and columns to a release.json entry written before 0.11.0. The export passes the store’s lookup; data-raw/run_place_exact.R reads <out dir>/species/species.parquet (or OBIS_SPECIES_LOOKUP) and fails when the species do not sum to the indicators.
  • collection.json for the h3 profile 1.1, with the atlas hooks. obis_h3_stac_collection() now writes the collection with id obis_h3 (was obis-h3; the atlas names it ?c=obis_h3) for profile https://oceanmetrics.io/schemas/h3/v1.1.0/schema.json: h3:periods as two period sets (decades at res_decade, years at res_year, each with its template), h3:layout.row_group_rows, h3:species_table.columns with name_key, year_min, year_max and the decade variant’s period, h3:heads ({layer: "taxon"}), cube:dimensions (layer: all and the EOVs; indicator; period: all, decades as <yyy0>s, years; res), atlas:metric (es), item_assets, and one STAC Item per map layer (items/<all|eov>.json, with data, decade and year assets: a folder and the path template under it). stats.parquet is the asset with role legend, taxon_groups.parquet the one with role search. New argument items.
  • New obis_h3_stac_stable(release_dir, base_url) writes the copy for a stable url, obis-h3/collection.json, with every href and template absolute under the release folder; data-raw/refresh_obis_h3.sh writes it after latest.json (step g2), validated with om-catalog validate h3 (exit 5 when it fails). Both validate against the 1.1 schema (jsonvalidate and the node CLI), with counter-fixtures (a period set without placeholder, year_min without year_max) failing.
  • Fix: taxon_groups.parquet no longer fails for a taxon layer without res 1.

obisindicators 0.10.1

  • New obis_h3_add_place_exact(release_dir, coll, source, manifest): registers a place_exact/coll=<coll>/ collection written into a release that was built without it (or without that collection), for example the gazetteer places (the 18 national marine sanctuaries) computed with data-raw/run_place_exact.R on a staging copy of the published release. release.json gets the collection under layers$place_exact$collections (from its meta.json) and the layer’s rows, files and bytes over every collection on disk; files.parquet has its place_exact rows replaced by one row per file on disk and files$n_files is updated (manifest = FALSE leaves it alone). Other layers, stats.parquet and a hand-edited layer note are untouched, and a second call gives the same files.
  • The exact place layer’s template, columns and note in release.json come from one internal helper shared by the export and the new function.

obisindicators 0.10.0

  • Year layers. obis_h3_export_parquet() writes year/all/year=<yyyy>/res=<r>/data_0.parquet and year/eov/eov=<eov>/year=<yyyy>/res=<r>/data_0.parquet: the decade layers per year, one partition per year present from min(date_year) to max(date_year). New arguments res_year (default 1-5; integer(0) skips them) and years (default NULL, every year). The SQL is the new exported obis_h3_year_sql(), built on the same indicator SQL as idx_h3 and the decade layers (which now share its builder). release.json gains layers.year_all, layers.year_eov, res_year, years (the years written), year_range and year_note; files.parquet and stats.parquet cover them.
  • stats.parquet has a year column (NA outside the year layers), so its rows are one per layer x key x decade x year x res x variable.
  • The species x hex x count table (layer species, sized and checked against h3t in spike 2 of the Ocean Metrics restructure), so a browser answers a WoRMS subtree or a cell’s species list from static files: species/res=<r>/class=<class>/data_0.parquet with columns h3, cell_id, name_key, aphiaid, n (n = records) at the resolutions res_species (default 3, 4, 5; res 4 rolled up from the res-5 tier), one file per (res, class), sorted by cell_id, aphiaid in row groups of 100k (ZSTD); a NULL class is written class=_none, since DuckDB-WASM reads __HIVE_DEFAULT_PARTITION__ as a string. species/species.parquet is the lookup, one row per aphiaid with name_key (a dense integer per species name: richness counts names, as h3t does), the OBIS ranks, lineage (the aphiaid then its ancestors up the store’s taxon table, walked from the occurrence’s own aphiaid, so a synonym keeps its own parent) and records. species/heads.json lists the taxa that still need a pre-aggregated head (Animalia and every taxon spanning two or more named classes: 125 in the v20261012 global store); the heads themselves are not built in this version. species_decades = TRUE also writes species_decade/res=<r>/decade=<d>/class=<class>/data_0.parquet (default off). A store without aphiaids (the demo store built from occ_SAtlantic) gets no species layer.
  • New exported functions for the table, each tested on a synthetic store: obis_h3_species_sql(), obis_h3_species_lookup_sql(), obis_h3_species_heads(), obis_h3_write_partitions() (the explicit per-partition writer: DuckDB’s PARTITION_BY wrote thousands of files per resolution and lost the sort) and obis_h3_species_subtree_sql() (a subtree’s indicators from the exported files, which reproduce the h3t subtree SQL cell for cell: n and sp exactly, Shannon, Simpson and ES to 1e-9).
  • collection.json: the export writes a STAC Collection of the release for the Ocean Metrics h3 profile, obis_h3_stac_collection(), with h3:species_table for the species layer and the other layers under obis:layers. It validates against h3.schema.json (tested with jsonvalidate and with om-catalog validate h3 when the platform checkout is present).
  • release.json’s layers.species carries the h3:species_table fields (href_template, resolutions, partition_by, sorted_by, columns, lookup) plus name_key, null_class, heads, the column types and the rows, files and bytes per resolution (by_res).
  • The place and place_exact layers of 0.8.0 and 0.9.0 are unchanged: they stay out of stats.parquet, and collection.json lists them under obis:layers.

obisindicators 0.9.0

  • New obis_place_indicators_exact(): indicators per place from the OBIS occurrences inside the true polygon, with no H3 approximation. It takes the occurrences (a data frame, or OBIS open-data parquet files, nested or flat, filtered as build_obis_h3_duckdb() does) and the places (an sf object or a GeoParquet with place_id and WKB geometry, such as a gazetteer places.parquet), splits each polygon into its parts and cuts them into quadrants until every piece has at most max_vertices (default 256) vertices (a place split at +/-180 gets local parts, so memory stays a few times the geometry size), joins every distinct location to the pieces with DuckDB spatial, and computes the indicators with the same SQL as the store’s layers. Polygons split at +/-180 work as they are. Returns indicators (place x eov x decade; eov is "all" or an EOV from the eov membership given as a data frame or a store connection; decade NA = all years), years (place x eov x year) and diagnostics. Columns: n, sp, shannon, simpson, es, hill_1 (exp(shannon)), hill_2 (1 / simpson), bp (Berger-Parker, max(ni) / n) and density (n / area_km2, records per km2, from area_km2 or the geodesic polygon area). diagnostics holds records_in, records_out and records_total (inside plus outside equals the total unless places overlap), records_in_unique and the overlapping locations with their place_ids, which also raise a warning. Resource guards (memory_limit, threads, temp_dir, max_temp_dir_size) as in build_obis_h3_duckdb(). The results equal calc_indicators() on the points inside the polygon (tested for all taxa, per decade, per year and for each of the seven EOVs).
  • New obis_place_exact_write() writes that result as place_exact/coll=<coll>/indicators.parquet and years.parquet (ZSTD, values only, no geometry) plus a meta.json (places, rows, record totals, overlaps, package version).
  • obis_h3_export_parquet() gains place_exact (a named list of slug = places GeoParquet; default NULL, no change), place_exact_occ (the occurrence parquet files), temp_dir and max_temp_dir_size: the exact place tables are written to place_exact/coll=<slug>/ in the release and listed in files.parquet (layer place_exact) and release.json (layers$place_exact); stats.parquet does not cover them. The monthly refresh turns it on with OBIS_PLACE_EXACT_COLLECTIONS="<slug> ...", reading $PLACES_INTERNAL/<slug>/places.parquet (default /share/data/places-internal), passed through, and mounted read-only, by run_refresh_docker.sh. data-raw/run_place_exact.R runs the same computation standalone.
  • obis_place_indicators_exact() takes max_vertices instead of grid_deg (deprecated: ignored, with a message). The 1 degree grid clip repeated each place’s whole geometry in every cell of its bounding box, which ran out of memory on EEZs and high seas that span +/-180; the quadrant subdivision writes one table per round and copies a geometry at most four times. diagnostics reports max_vertices, max_piece_vertices and subdivision_rounds instead of grid_deg; data-raw/run_place_exact.R reads OBIS_MAX_VERTICES.
  • No change to the indicator math or to the output of any existing function.

obisindicators 0.8.0

  • New obis_place_indicators(): indicators per place, pooled from area-weighted H3 cells. It takes a place-cell membership (place_id, h3, share, as the Ocean Metrics gazetteer publishes it per collection) and, for each place, sums every species’ records over the member cells weighted by the cell’s share of area inside the place (ni = sum(records * share); the gazetteer keeps shares of at least 1%), then computes n, sp, Shannon, Simpson and ES(50) with the store’s indicator SQL. Layers all and eov (per EOV), each for all years and per decade (1960-2020, as the export’s decade layers); also cells (member cells with records) and area (their summed share). These are true per-place indices of the pooled, area-weighted counts, not means of hexagon values: n is fractional because of the weighting, richness counts every species with any weighted record inside the place, and ES(50) is NA where the weighted n is below 50.
  • New obis_place_membership() resolves a gazetteer collection (slug, directory, URL or membership.json) to its membership parquet files at one resolution.
  • obis_h3_export_parquet() gains place_collections (default NULL, no change): a named list of collections, each written as one file place/coll=<slug>/data_0.parquet with every place, layer and decade, listed in files.parquet (layer place) and release.json (layers$place, with each collection’s membership version). stats.parquet does not cover it. The monthly refresh turns it on with OBIS_PLACE_COLLECTIONS="<slug> ..." (optionally GAZETTEER_BASE), passed through by run_refresh_docker.sh.
  • The shared indicator SQL (.h3t_indicators_sql()) is documented for fractional counts; it needed no change, and integer results are unchanged.

obisindicators 0.7.3

  • release.json’s obis_snapshot is the OBIS data date, the date of the newest object in s3://obis-open-data/occurrence/ the store was built from, not the date the refresh ran. OBIS updates that folder one dataset at a time and publishes no export date, so refresh_obis_h3.sh reads it off the synced files (which aws s3 sync stamps with their S3 LastModified) and passes it as OBIS_DATA_DATE; without it, the date in the release tag is used as before. For v20261012 that is 2026-10-11 (synced 2026-10-12). The release tag stays the sync date.
  • latest.json also carries worms_version, the ChecklistBank WoRMS version the taxonomy came from.

obisindicators 0.7.2

  • Family is a precomputed taxon rank. H3T_IDX_RANKS gains "family", so the store’s idx_h3_taxon and the export’s taxon/rank=family/ layer carry every family (about 5,800 in the v20260728 store), and a single-family h3t query takes the precomputed path. migrate_add_idx_h3_taxon.R adds it to an existing store.
  • The monthly obis-h3 refresh runs in Docker on the Mac mini. New data-raw/docker/Dockerfile (R 4.6.1, CRAN from a dated Posit Package Manager snapshot, duckdb 1.5.5, the h3/spatial/httpfs extensions, AWS CLI v2) and data-raw/run_refresh_docker.sh (Colima VM started and stopped per run, data on the external drive mounted at /share/data, the new store rsynced to msens for h3t). refresh_obis_h3.sh runs R directly when BUILD_CONTAINER is empty (inside the image); msens’s docker exec plumber mode is unchanged.
  • refresh_obis_h3.sh sources every file in R/ for the export: the subset it sourced before lacked eov.R, so the export stopped at taxon_groups (could not find function "obis_eov_label").
  • obis_h3_export_parquet() computes stats.parquet one layer and variable at a time: the single UNPIVOT over every layer held all values in quantile_cont() states at once and, with the family rank, was killed for lack of memory in a 24 GiB VM. Same rows, values and column types (regression test).
  • The WoRMS taxonomy is refreshed by the monthly run. New step (a2) in refresh_obis_h3.sh: when the version of ChecklistBank dataset 2011 (WoRMS’s monthly DwC-A, public) differs from taxon.parquet.json, it downloads the archive, runs build_taxon_parquet.R and records the version, which release.json carries as worms_version. New flags --skip-taxonomy and --taxonomy-only. The build’s gap-fill of AphiaIDs missing from the download (WoRMS REST) is unchanged. run_refresh_docker.sh skips a separate mount for a checkout that sits inside the data folder (Colima refuses overlapping mounts).
  • release.json’s obisindicators_version comes from the checkout’s DESCRIPTION when OBIS_PKG_ROOT is set (.obisindicators_version()), so the image needs no installed package.

obisindicators 0.7.1

  • obis_h3_export_parquet() splits the fine resolutions by parent cell, so a browser loads only the cells covering its viewport instead of a whole 33 MB all/res=7 file. New arguments parent_res (default c("6" = 2L, "7" = 3L): res 6 by its res-2 parent, res 7 by its res-3 parent, for the all and eov layers), parent_res_taxon (default the res-0 base cell, which keeps the taxon layer to thousands rather than millions of files), parent_min_rows (default 50000: smaller (layer key, res) partitions stay whole) and max_open (partitions per COPY). Split partitions are written to .../res=<r>/p=<parent h3>/data_0.parquet; res 1-5 and the decade layers stay whole. files.parquet gains a parent column (NULL for whole files) and release.json documents each layer’s parent_res and the rule (parents).
  • New data-raw/refresh_obis_h3.sh: the monthly obis-h3 release pipeline (sync OBIS open data, build the store, obis_h3_export_parquet(), validate against the previous release, upload to S3, then write obis-h3/latest.json). Scheduled from oceanmetrics/erddap-places on the msens runner; documented in data-raw/README.md. Supports --skip-sync/-build/-export/-upload, --release and --dry-run.

obisindicators 0.7.0

  • New obis_h3_export_parquet(): export a store to hive-partitioned Parquet for a serverless web app (static hosting + DuckDB-WASM + deck.gl H3HexagonLayer). Writes <dir_out>/<release>/ with all/res=N/ (idx_h3), eov/eov=<eov>/res=N/ (idx_h3_eov), taxon/rank=<rank>/taxon=<taxon>/res=N/ (idx_h3_taxon), and two layers computed from occ_h3 per decade (decade/all/decade=<yyy0>/res=N/, decade/eov/eov=<eov>/decade=<yyy0>/res=N/; res 1-5 and decades 1960-2020 by default). Every file has h3 (lowercase hex string), cell_id, n, sp, shannon, simpson, es. Also writes stats.parquet (min, 2nd, 50th, 98th percentile, max and cell count per layer x key x res x variable, for colour ramps), taxon_groups.parquet (the taxa and EOVs on offer, with totals and on-disk / URL paths), files.parquet (a manifest of every file with its row count and size, since HTTP cannot glob) and release.json (release, snapshot, package and DuckDB versions, row counts per layer, layout and columns). Each partition is exactly one data_0.parquet; the taxon layer is written in batches of at most 100 partitions per COPY to stay under the OS open-file limit. Partition values are percent-encoded by DuckDB; url_path gives the form to fetch over HTTP.
  • The indicator SQL behind idx_h3, idx_h3_taxon and idx_h3_eov now comes from one internal builder (.h3t_indicators_sql()), which the decade layers of the export reuse. The output of the store build is unchanged.
  • jsonlite added to Suggests (used by the export).

obisindicators 0.6.1

  • Precomputed store articles: the figures now show on the pkgdown site (and in the paper/ gallery on GitHub). The vignettes that query an obis_h3 store (scaling, taxon_children) rendered code-only (eval = FALSE) because the store is not available on GitHub Actions. They move to vignettes/articles/ (pkgdown-only, excluded from the package build) as *.Rmd.orig sources that data-raw/precompute_articles.R knits locally against a store into committed *.Rmd + figures/; CI renders those as-is. The tile maps stay live.
    • The paper/ Quarto notebooks are folded into the articles, which now double as the manuscript’s figure notebooks: scaling (Tables 2, 5; Fig. 3), taxon_children (Table 3; Fig. 4), and new articles eov (Table 4; Figs. 1–2), decadal (Fig. 5) and places (Fig. 6). Each article saves its manuscript figure + CSV to paper/figures/ (now committed) via paper/_common.R; paper/README.md is the figure gallery and index.
    • Site navigation: articles are grouped into “Shipped data” and “The obis_h3 store”. No changes to exported functions.
  • Analysis-side helpers for the paper’s figures and case studies — the tile-SQL builders now have data-frame counterparts, so every figure in paper/ is a call to a tested, exported function rather than notebook code. No new indicator math: everything runs the SQL already pinned to calc_indicators() / calc_spue(), or calls those references directly.
    • Store (R/store.R): obis_store_connect() (read-only + LOAD h3), obis_store_stats() (tables, totals, cells by resolution — Table 2), obis_h3t_query() (run any tile SQL at a fixed resolution, keyed on the hex string), obis_cell_indicators() (n/sp/shannon/es per cell for any filter, reading idx_h3 / idx_h3_eov when it can), obis_bench() + obis_bench_queries() (cold/warm timings of the four serving paths), h3_res_table().
    • Scale (R/scale.R): calc_scale_curves() and calc_spue_scale() — occupied cells, records-per-cell quantiles, ES-eligible fraction, medians and reliability floors across H3 resolutions (Fig. 3).
    • Comparisons (R/compare.R): calc_rank_vs_subtree() + obis_rank_presets() (records by DwC rank column vs AphiaID subtree — Table 3), calc_eov_totals() + compare_eov_totals() (per-EOV totals and before/after a taxonomy change — Table 4), calc_spue_cells(), h3_raster_to_cells() (aggregate an SDM raster to H3 by pixel centres or hexagon centroids) and compare_spue_sdm() (Spearman + calibration bins, effort-gated — Fig. 4).
    • Periods (R/temporal.R): calc_period_indicators() and calc_period_change() (decadal ES50/richness per cell, change where both decades are reliable — Fig. 5).
    • Places (R/place.R): place_cells() and calc_place_indicators() (roll H3 cells up to sanctuary/EEZ polygons and compute indicators with calc_indicators() — Fig. 6).
    • Visualize (R/visualize.R): hex_sf() (cells → dateline-wrapped polygons), gmap_cells() (map a per-cell table with an optional reliability mask), plot_scale_curves(), plot_spue_sdm(); gmap_indicator() gains a bbox argument and drops the deprecated aes_string().
    • Tests: tests/testthat/test-paper-helpers.R on a new synthetic fixture (helper-paper.R: turtles + birds with DwC ranks and years, baked idx_h3 and idx_h3_eov) asserts exact values for every helper, including precomputed-vs-live agreement of obis_cell_indicators().
    • paper/: Quarto notebooks, one per figure/table (store stats + benchmarks, rank vs subtree, gap-fill EOV totals, EOV maps, scale curves, SPUE vs SDM, decadal change, place roll-ups), driven by OBIS_H3_DUCKDB; plus paper/build_demo_store.R to build a regional demo store (Gulf of Mexico + Caribbean) from a local OBIS export and a WoRMS table.
    • Suggests: terra (raster aggregation), patchwork (figure panels).

obisindicators 0.5.0

  • Essential Ocean Variables (EOVs) — new R/eov.R maps the GOOS/IOOS biology & ecosystems EOVs onto the H3 store. The IOOS Marine Life Data Network defines each EOV as a handful of root WoRMS AphiaIDs (33 seeds across 7 EOVs: fish, hardCorals, mangroves, marineMammals, seabirds, seagrasses, seaTurtles), which is exactly a multi-seed version of the existing subtree walk.

    • obis_eov_seeds() / obis_eov_aphiaid() — the EOV definitions.
    • obis_eov_sql() — tile SQL for an EOV, routing to a precomputed layer when it can and to the live AphiaID-subtree path when it must (year filters, several EOVs at once, or a store without the layer baked).
    • obis_eov_bake() — adds eov (membership) and idx_h3_eov (precomputed indicators, res 1-7) to a store; now also a step in build_obis_h3_duckdb(), skipped with a note when taxon is absent.
    • New driver data-raw/migrate_add_eov.R.

  • WoRMS gap-fill — new R/taxon_gapfill.R closes a silent coverage hole. The bulk WoRMS taxon.txt download is not a complete cover of the AphiaIDs OBIS carries: on the 2026-07 global store 12,021 of 167,190 distinct occ_h3.aphiaid values (~7%, covering 8.3M of 121.9M records) were absent from taxon, so they were invisible to every aphiaid / EOV / SPUE query.

    • obis_taxon_orphans() — report the gap.
    • wm_aphia_records() — batched, parallel WoRMS REST lookups (AphiaRecordsByAphiaIDs, 50 ids/request), the per-id supplement to the bulk download.
    • obis_taxon_fill_gaps() — fills orphans and iterates to transitive closure, because inserting an orphan whose ancestors are still missing leaves it disconnected from any seed above it. Warns and reports closed = FALSE rather than implying a whole tree if max_rounds is hit.
    • New driver data-raw/migrate_fill_taxon_gaps.R.
    • Adds httr2 to Suggests.

  • Two taxon-group presets in the h3-db app returned zero records (fixed in MarineSensitivity/apps/h3-db, noted here because it motivated the EOV design): filtering the DwC class column cannot match when WoRMS files the name at another rank — class='Actinopterygii' (a Gigaclass; OBIS’s class is Teleostei, 44.2M records) and class='Anthozoa' (a Subphylum; OBIS uses Hexacorallia/Octocorallia) both matched nothing. AphiaID subtree walking is rank-agnostic and immune to this.

  • Parity: .h3t_idx_eov_sql() is a fifth copy of the calc_indicators() ES(n) term and is pinned cell-for-cell by the new tests/testthat/test-eov-parity.R.

obisindicators 0.4.2

  • Vignette H3 tile maps now actually render (the mapgl/MapLibre chunks that 0.4.1 still left as code-only):
    • vignette("h3t") renders the interactive ES50 hexagon map; vignette("taxon_children") renders the Cetacea-records map and the SPUE map. These are client-side MapLibre widgets — tiles are fetched from the deployed h3t service in the reader’s browser, so they need no store/S3 at build time.
    • New Remote dependency: the maps require the h3t-antimeridian fix in mapgl (renders H3 hexagons that cross the dateline), pinned via Remotes: mapgl=bbest/mapgl@fix/h3t-antimeridian (walkerke/mapgl#211). Switch to upstream mapgl once that PR merges.
    • Fixed a latent bug in the h3t map example — interpolate(values=) now has the same length as stops= (a 3-stop viridis ramp), which previously would have errored had the chunk been evaluated.
    • vignette("scaling") stays code-only: every chunk runs live benchmark queries against the deployed DuckDB store (no map widgets), which CI cannot reach.

obisindicators 0.4.1

  • Vignettes now render their evaluable R chunks on the pkgdown site instead of showing code-only:
    • vignette("h3") runs the full h3-grid → calc_indicators() → gmap_indicator() pipeline on shipped occ_1M and renders the ES(50) map (only the deckgl install/demo stays code-only).
    • vignette("taxon_children") now renders the generated WITH RECURSIVE tile SQL and tile URLs from obis_h3t_sql(aphiaid=) / obis_spue_sql() (pure builders, no store needed); only the DB-connection and mapgl widget chunks stay code-only.
    • vignette("h3t") suppresses package-load messages so the evaluated obis_h3t_sql() output is clean.
    • Chunks that genuinely require the deployed S3 / DuckDB store / h3t tile service (vignette("scaling"), the build/deploy/map chunks) remain illustrative code, as they cannot run in CI.

obisindicators 0.4.0

  • Automatic per-tile spatial pruning via hex_prune (supersedes 0.3.0’s client-side {{bbox}} placeholder). The tile bbox is fully determined by the z/x/y tile address, so the client no longer states it — the h3t server derives each tile’s covering coarse H3 cells from z/x/y and injects the prune itself:
    • build_obis_h3_duckdb() now materializes a coarse H3-parent column hex_prune = h3_cell_to_parent(cell_id, LEAST(res, H3T_PRUNE_RES)) (res 3) on occ_h3 and idx_h3 and clusters both by (res, hex_prune, cell_id). This replaces the interim lat/lng clustering — pruning on the H3 index is 2D (tighter than a latitude band), needs no extra float columns, and the covering ids are canonical H3 (they match across the R build and the server with no version drift). Store schema change — rebuild, or migrate with data-raw/migrate_add_spatial_cluster.R (drops lat/lng, adds hex_prune).
    • obis_h3t_sql() / obis_spue_sql() now emit plain per-resolution SELECTs — the bbox_placeholder argument is removed. The server (MarineSensitivity/server/h3t, CalCOFI/api-h3t-py) rewrites the query to add hex_prune IN (<covering cells>) to any scan of a table carrying that column; stores without it are untouched.
    • The math is unchanged and still pinned to calc_indicators() / calc_spue(); test-h3t-prune.R asserts the prune is result-preserving (a hex_prune-pruned scan + the server’s outer centroid filter returns exactly the same cells and values as the unpruned scan).

obisindicators 0.3.0

  • Spatial (bbox) tile pruning (interim — the {{bbox}} placeholder and lat/lng clustering here were replaced by the hex_prune approach in 0.4.0; kept for history). Live occ_h3 / idx_h3 tile maps were pruned per tile instead of aggregating the whole globe for every tile:
    • build_obis_h3_duckdb() materialized cell-centroid lat/lng columns on occ_h3 and idx_h3 and clustered both by (res, lat, lng).
    • obis_h3t_sql() / obis_spue_sql() gained a bbox_placeholder argument (default "{{bbox}}") that the h3t service substituted per tile with a lat/lng predicate.
    • The math stayed pinned to calc_indicators() / calc_spue(); the prune was asserted result-preserving.

obisindicators 0.2.0

  • Added WoRMS taxonomy children resolution and an effort proxy (SPUE) so OBIS can be filtered by any WoRMS AphiaID at any rank from the local snapshot (see vignette("taxon_children"), vignette("scaling")):
    • obis_taxon_children() / obis_taxon_subtree_sql() recursively walk a taxon table (baked into the store; data-raw/build_taxon_parquet.R + data-raw/migrate_add_taxon.R) to return every descendant taxon.
    • obis_h3t_sql(aphiaid=) serves arbitrary-rank children maps by filtering occ_h3.aphiaid to the resolved subtree via a WITH RECURSIVE CTE.
    • calc_spue() (R reference) + obis_spue_sql() compute the presence-only effort proxy records(target subtree) / records(effort subtree) per cell, pinned by test-spue-parity.R.
  • Added an H3 tiling (h3t) workflow to serve indicators as on-demand H3 hexagon map tiles (see vignette("h3t")):
    • build_obis_h3_duckdb() builds an authoritative DuckDB store from OBIS open-data parquet — a precomputed all-taxa indicator layer (idx_h3, res 1–7) plus a species-level store (occ_h3, tiers 3/5/7) for on-the-fly taxon/year-filtered queries. The ES50/Shannon/Simpson/richness math is the SQL translation of calc_indicators(), pinned by a new parity test.
    • obis_h3t_sql() / obis_h3t_url() compose the validated read-only SELECT and the base64-encoded tile URL for the h3t service (MarineSensitivity/server/h3t) and mapgl::add_h3t_source().
    • canonical SQL in inst/sql/; server build driver in data-raw/build_obis_h3_duckdb.R.

obisindicators 0.0.2

  • Renamed functions for consistency:
    • calc_es50() -> calc_indicators()
    • gmap_metric() -> gmap_indicator()
  • Fixed gmap_indicator() to use default Robinson projection.
  • Updated vignettes with name changes and use of “indicators” over “metrics”.
  • Supplemented documentation for calc_indicators() with expected input and output columns to data frame.
  • Added documentation for occ_fk and occ_1960s to occ_2010s
  • Made generation of occ_* datasets more reproducible with set.seed() and sampled versions of dataset to minimize file size on Github in data-raw/occ.R.

obisindicators 0.0.1

  • Added a NEWS.md file to track changes to the package.
